name: Amílcar Cabral International Airport
before:
Cape Verde's main international airport, on Sal, 2 km from Espargos and on the road down to Santa Maria where most of the resorts are. It is the hub for Cabo Verde Airlines and the base for Cabo Verde Express.

Transfers need arranging. There is no scheduled public transport at all, so it is taxis, hire cars or the shared cars known locally as aluguer.

The runway is 3,272 metres, the longest in the country, which is what allows the long haul flying. It was also one of the designated emergency landing strips for the Space Shuttle, and the airport was one of NASA's chosen sites to handle a Shuttle after re-entry.

The terminal is a single two storey building and passengers are bussed out to the aircraft. Duty free, kiosks and refreshments sit beyond security and passport control.

It has been an airport since 1939, built by Italy as a fuel and provisions stop on the route from Europe to South America, with the first flight arriving from Rome and Seville that December.
after:
Cape Verde's main international airport, on Sal, 2 km from Espargos, with direct flights to Europe.

Transfers need arranging. Taxis meet arrivals and there are hire car desks. The FCDO advises using only authorised taxis, which on Sal are blue and yellow. Informal shared minibuses also run on the island.

The airport dates from 1939, when it was built as an Italian airfield. It has the longest runway in Cape Verde.

According to the FCDO, visitors must pre-register and pay the airport security fee (TSA) online at least five days before arrival, and since 1 July 2026 anyone who cannot show proof pays double at the border.

claims.note: The operator's 2025 traffic table (VINCI Airports, in thousands of passengers) gives Sal 1,588, Praia 753, Boa Vista 670 and São Vicente 354. No second source for the figure itself was found (INE Cabo Verde's tables are script-driven and the Cape Verdean papers reached have no usable index), so no passenger number is stated, as the drafting note allowed.

claims.claim: FCDO: pre-register and pay the TSA online five days ahead; double at the border from 1 July 2026
claims.inAfter: According to the FCDO, visitors must pre-register and pay the airport security fee (TSA) online at least five days before arrival, and since 1 July 2026 anyone who cannot show proof pays double at the border.
claims.note: Added: it will catch travellers out and the penalty is new. Attributed statement, checked against the FCDO's Cape Verde entry page (guide updated 28 July 2026, still current 23 September 2026). The FCDO adds that children aged one and under are exempt and that tour operators may do it for the traveller; not stated.

sources.org: UK FCDO (Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office)
quote: You must fill in a traveller entry form at least 5 days before you arrive in the country. Complete the pre-registration and pay the airport security fee ('TSA') on the official online platform. Bring proof of confirmation to show when you arrive.
From 1 July 2026, if you do not complete the pre-registration or cannot show proof, you will have to pay double the TSA fee at border control.

claims.claim: on the road down to Santa Maria where most of the resorts are
claims.wasBefore: and on the road down to Santa Maria where most of the resorts are
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator's Sal page names Santa Maria only for its pier; a September 2026 report places one resort (the Hilton) in Santa Maria and RIU names its three Sal hotels, but no source reached says most resorts are there or describes the road. The Sal municipality's site reset the connection and then presented a self-signed certificate, so it was left.

claims.wasBefore: It is the hub for Cabo Verde Airlines
claims.why: Out of date or at least unconfirmed. Cabo Verde Airlines' own site (live, 23 September 2026) features only routes from Praia (Lisbon, Providence, Recife) and offers check-in from Praia, São Vicente and Sal alike; Wikipedia's hub label dates from the 2019 Sal hub. Replaced by the direct flights to Europe.

claims.wasBefore: and the base for Cabo Verde Express
claims.why: No current source. The operator's airline list (live, 23 September 2026) does not include Cabo Verde Express; Wikipedia alone says it is based here.

claims.claim: no scheduled public transport at all
claims.wasBefore: There is no scheduled public transport at all, so it is taxis, hire cars or the shared cars known locally as aluguer.
claims.why: Taxis, hire cars and informal shared transport are kept with the operator's pages. 'No scheduled public transport at all' rests on Wikipedia alone: the operator says only that informal services in some cases replace taxis and buses.

claims.claim: runway 3,272 metres, which allows the long-haul flying
claims.wasBefore: The runway is 3,272 metres, the longest in the country, which is what allows the long haul flying.
claims.why: 'Longest in the country' is kept. The length is disputed (operator 3,000 m, Wikipedia 3,272 m, OurAirports 3,280 m), and the link to long-haul flying is Wikipedia's alone.

claims.claim: Space Shuttle emergency landing strip; NASA site
claims.wasBefore: It was also one of the designated emergency landing strips for the Space Shuttle, and the airport was one of NASA's chosen sites to handle a Shuttle after re-entry.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and history of no use for booking (the Shuttle retired in 2011).

claims.claim: single two-storey terminal; bussed to aircraft; duty free after security
claims.wasBefore: The terminal is a single two storey building and passengers are bussed out to the aircraft. Duty free, kiosks and refreshments sit beyond security and passport control.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator says the terminals were modernised in its first phase of works, finished in 2025, and that a new three-year phase (from January 2026) includes terminal expansions, so the description may already be out of date.

claims.claim: 1939 fuel stop on the Europe to South America route; first flight from Rome and Seville in December
claims.wasBefore: It has been an airport since 1939, built by Italy as a fuel and provisions stop on the route from Europe to South America, with the first flight arriving from Rome and Seville that December.
claims.why: The 1939 Italian origin is kept with the operator. The purpose and the first flight (15 December 1939, from Rome and Seville) rest on Wikipedia alone.
Not in the Overview, and none is added: Wikipedia says both 'four gates' and 'six departure gates', and the operator gives no count, as the drafting note required.

opinion.why: Advice kept from the old text; follows from the taxi, hire car and minibus options.
